benchmarks: Deep Memory Retrieval (DMR, from MemGPT), LongMemEval
fallos_mitigaciones: Temporally overlapping contradictions between new and existing edges (stale/superseded facts) mitigated by LLM-driven edge invalidation prioritizing the transactional timeline T' (new info wins), §2.2.3. The paper also self-critiques the DMR benchmark's own limitations (ambiguous questions, small scale, poor enterprise representativeness, §4.2), motivating the harder LongMemEval evaluation.
cita: Rasmussen et al. (2025). Zep: A Temporal Knowledge Graph Architecture for Agent Memory.
notes: mem_tipos EPISODICA;SEMANTICA: explicit dual episode-subgraph (raw messages, non-lossy) + semantic-entity-subgraph (resolved entities/facts), directly mirrors 'psychological models of human memory... episodic memory... semantic memory' (§2). representacion=GRAFO;VECTOR: temporal knowledge graph G=(N,E,phi) with 3 tiers (episode/semantic/community subgraphs, §2) + entity/fact/community names embedded for cosine search (§2.2.1, §2.3). operaciones=WRITE;CONSOLIDACION;ACTUALIZACION: episode ingestion + entity/fact extraction (WRITE, §2.1-2.2); community subgraph built via community detection + iterative map-reduce summarization (CONSOLIDACION, §2.3); temporal extraction and EDGE INVALIDATION -- 'the system employs an LLM to compare new edges against semantically related existing edges to identify potential contradictions...invalidates the affected edges' (ACTUALIZACION, §2.2.3). trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA;CHECKPOINT: ingestion per episode/message; 'periodic community refreshes remain necessary' (CHECKPOINT, §2.3). retrieval=EMBEDDINGS;GREP-ARCHIVOS;GRAFO;RANKING: cosine semantic similarity, Okapi BM25 full-text, breadth-first graph search (§3.1); rerankers RRF/MMR/cross-encoder/episode-mentions/node-distance (§3.2). mide_lectura=SI (matches F_screening): DMR and LongMemEval accuracy explicitly measured (Table1-3). alcance=SESION: DMR is 5-session conversations; LongMemEval has an explicit 'cross-session information synthesis' category. fidelidad_procedencia=SI: bi-temporal model with tvalid/tinvalid/t'created/t'expired tracking fact validity over time, LLM-driven contradiction detection and edge invalidation (§2.2.3). F=RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO;FIDELIDAD;COSTO (matches F_screening, confirmed). evidencia_tipo=BENCHMARK-E2E(Table1-3)+MEDICION-COSTO(latency/tokens, Table2) -- no explicit internal component ablation of Zep's own modules was found in the reviewed text. handoff=CONTENIDO: facts/entities persist and are retrieved across sessions ('cross-session information synthesis', Abstract).

benchmarks: HumanEval, HumanEval-ET, EvalPlus, MBPP, MBPP-ET, APPS, xCodeEval, CodeContest
fallos_mitigaciones: Prior external-storage approaches 'either store the complete responses directly...or summarize all the content before storing...requir[ing] excessive storage space or result[ing] in content loss due to summarization' (§1); mitigated by Cogito's region-specific hippocampus-inspired storage (different content types retained per CA region, tokenizer-compression only at CA4).
cita: Li et al. (2025). Cogito, ergo sum: A Neurobiologically-Inspired Cognition-Memory-Growth System for Code Generation.
notes: mem_tipos=EPISODICA;PROCEDIMENTAL: CA1/CA3 store per-attempt responses and code-version+error-traceback history (episodic records of past attempts, §3.3); the Super-Role's accumulated cross-role 'knowledge and cognitive skills' constitute reusable problem-solving strategy (procedural). representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS: plain-text/code stored in named hippocampus-inspired regions (CA1/CA2/CA3/CA4) with numeric importance-score/weight metadata (Fig.2); no concrete vector-embedding-based or graph-based retrieval mechanism is described despite the paper's qualitative claim of 'quick retrieval in similar tasks' -- hence retrieval is marked NA. operaciones=WRITE;ADMISION;CONSOLIDACION: responses stored per CA region (WRITE); Fig.2 shows candidate content filtered by importance-score x weight against a MIN threshold before being retained (ADMISION); CA4 'utilize a tokenizer to reduce the size of the stored content, optimizing memory space' (CONSOLIDACION, §3.3). trigger=PRESUPUESTO: importance-score x weight vs MIN threshold gates retention (Fig.2, §3.4). retrieval=NA: no concrete IR mechanism (embeddings/grep/graph/ranking) is described. mide_lectura=SI (matches F_screening): Table3 ablation 'Cogito w/o Super-Role' (without carrying accumulated memory forward) shows the largest performance drop (69.33% vs 90.24% full), demonstrating the utility of reused memory. alcance=TAREA: the hippocampus-like memory operates within a SINGLE question's Debugger->Coder->Planner->Super-Role pipeline (Algorithm1). multiagente=SI: explicit multi-agent system where memory 'acts as a communication bridge across different groups, facilitating the transfer of knowledge and strategies' (§3.2). F=RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO;CONSOLIDACION;COSTO (matches F_screening, confirmed). handoff=CONTENIDO: the Super-Role's accumulated experience is explicitly a 'communication bridge across different groups' (§3.2) between the Debugger/Coder/Planner role-agents. plan_estado=NO: the Planner's output ('Plan') is stored as one type of role-experience content, not a meta-level task-progress tracker.

fallos_mitigaciones: 'No single LLM dominates across all programming languages, all problem categories, or all stages' (a model strong at Python generation may be weak at Rust or at debugging, Table1); mitigated by per-stage, per-category memory-informed routing (Table3, Observation1-2). Brute-force multi-model search is computationally prohibitive; mitigated by capping the candidate pool to top-k=5 ranked LLMs per the memory ranking (§3.2, sensitivity analysis §6.2).
cita: Chen et al. (2025). Multi-LLM Orchestration for High-Quality Code Generation: Exploiting Complementary Model Strengths.
notes: mem_tipos=PROCEDIMENTAL: the 'Memory module' is a ranking matrix of which LLM performs best per (language, category) -- reusable strategic know-how for task routing, not conversational/episodic content (§3.2-3.6). representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS: a structured offline-profiled ranking table/matrix indexed by language x category (Fig.3); the closest closed-vocab fit though not literally free text -- the vocabulary has no dedicated 'table/matrix' token. operaciones=WRITE;ACTUALIZACION: initial construction 'from offline profiling data' (WRITE) that is explicitly 'updatable as new models/versions become available' (ACTUALIZACION, Abstract, §1). trigger=CHECKPOINT: memory is built via a distinct OFFLINE profiling phase before deployment, not during live task execution (Abstract) -- closest to a periodic/scheduled batch process. retrieval=RANKING: 'each agent consults its Memory to select the most suitable LLMs' via the profiled ranking lookup, §3.2. mide_lectura=SI (matches F_screening): Table3 compares per-stage/per-category memory-informed routing against majority-voting and single-model baselines, measuring the improvement from consulting the memory (Observation1-2, §3.1). alcance=TAREA: the memory is consulted per individual coding problem/task at inference time. multiagente=SI: explicit 4-agent orchestration system (Categorization/Generation/Debugging/Refinement) where the Memory module is 'Used by Agent B/C/D' (Fig.3). F=WRITE;RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO;COSTO;MULTIAGENTE (MULTIAGENTE added vs F_screening for the dedicated multi-agent architecture where Memory is explicitly shared across the 4 agents, Fig.3). handoff=CONTENIDO: the profiled ranking memory (content) is consulted/shared by the Generation, Debugging, and Refinement agents within the same pipeline execution (Fig.3). plan_estado=NO.

fallos_mitigaciones: Existing LLM-based FL methods (SoapFL, AutoFL) 'depend on complex multi-agent systems or intricate LLM tool usage' and their effectiveness significantly declines on complex projects lacking project-specific context (e.g. Closure, Fig.1, §III); mitigated by MemFL's static+dynamic external memory injecting project-specific knowledge directly into a simplified 3-step pipeline (§III-IV).
cita: Yeo et al. (2025). Improving LLM-Based Fault Localization with External Memory and Project Context.
notes: mem_tipos=SEMANTICA;PROCEDIMENTAL: static memory = pre-generated project/class summaries (abstracted declarative facts about the codebase, §IV-A); dynamic memory = iteratively refined debugging guidance/strategy from prior fault-localization attempts (reusable how-to knowledge, §IV-A). representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS: plain-text summaries and guidance directly concatenated into the LLM prompt ('simply concatenating an external memory containing project-specific knowledge', §I); no vector/graph store. operaciones=WRITE;CONSOLIDACION;ACTUALIZACION: static memory generated once from source code (WRITE + CONSOLIDACION, summarizing raw code into project/class summaries, §IV-D1); dynamic memory 'is adaptive and evolves throughout the fault localization...iteratively refine Dynamic Memory' by comparing outputs against bug reports (ACTUALIZACION, §IV-A/B). trigger=DISCRECIONAL-LLM;CHECKPOINT: dynamic-memory refinement runs as a dedicated OFFLINE 'External Memory Generation' phase on a small training dataset before actual fault localization begins (CHECKPOINT-style precomputation, §IV-B), with the LLM itself judging/generating the guidance content (DISCRECIONAL-LLM). retrieval=NA: memory content is directly and wholly concatenated into the prompt at each of the 3 FL steps, not queried via similarity search. mide_lectura=SI (matches F_screening, interpreted broadly as measuring memory-content usage/utility): the paper explicitly conducts an ablation study isolating static-vs-dynamic memory contributions ('showed effectiveness of each component of MemFL through ablation study', §I). alcance=PROYECTO: static memory holds 'pre-generated summaries of the project and its classes' -- project-wide scope, reused across different bugs within the same project (§IV-A). multiagente=NO: MemFL is explicitly a simpler single-LLM 3-step pipeline, contrasted against the multi-agent baseline SoapFL (§II-C). F=RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO;COSTO (matches F_screening, confirmed under the broad reading above). handoff=CONTENIDO: the static+dynamic memory (content) persists and is reused across separate bug-localization runs for the SAME project. plan_estado=NO.

benchmarks: Stateful GSM-Symbolic (P1/P2), Stateful AIME (2024+2025), Multi-Query GSM-Symbolic
fallos_mitigaciones: Standard test-time compute treats problems as stateless, so multiple related queries about the same context force redundant recomputation, incurring extra latency/cost (§1); mitigated by sleep-time compute precomputing/amortizing inferences about the shared context offline, reducing test-time compute needed for equal accuracy by ~5x (§5.1) and cutting per-query cost up to 2.5x when amortized (§5.3). Acknowledged, unmitigated limitation: 'at the [highest] test-time compute budgets, the test-time-compute-only baseline slightly outperforms sleep-time compute' (§5.1).
cita: Lin et al. (2025). Sleep-time Compute: Beyond Inference Scaling at Test-time.
notes: mem_tipos=TRABAJO: the re-represented context c' is a precomputed enrichment of the IMMEDIATE working context available for an upcoming query, not a long-term store persisted across distinct sessions -- 'S(c) -> c'' operates on whatever context c is currently at hand (§3), closest to working-memory precomputation/caching. representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS: c' is plain LLM-generated re-written text (inferences and re-representations of c, §3, Appendix K); no vector/graph structure. operaciones=WRITE;CONSOLIDACION: S(c)->c' generates ('writes') a new derived context by drawing inferences and re-writing c (§3); also a form of CONSOLIDACION (distilling/enriching raw context into a denser reasoning-annotated form), though the paper does not use that term. trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA: sleep-time compute is deterministically triggered whenever context c is available and idle time precedes the query q ('during this time, the LLM is typically idling', §1). retrieval=NA: c' directly replaces c in the test-time prompt; no query-time search/retrieval mechanism over a store is described. mide_lectura=NO (matches F_screening 'COSTO' only): the paper measures compute/accuracy tradeoffs of the precomputed context, not retrieval precision. alcance=TAREA: experiments are on single context+question(s) reasoning tasks (Stateful GSM-Symbolic/AIME); the paper's motivating examples (coding agents across debugging rounds, conversational assistants maintaining dialogue, §1) suggest a SESION framing but are not what is actually benchmarked. F=WRITE;COSTO (WRITE added vs F_screening='COSTO' alone, since the core contribution IS the mechanism S(c)->c' that generates/writes a new precomputed context offline). handoff=CONTENIDO: the sleep-time-precomputed context c' is generated offline and later consumed at test-time, and can be shared/amortized across multiple related queries about the same context (§3, §5.3). plan_estado=NO.

fallos_mitigaciones: Without persistent memory, 'the system forgets critical user information...between sessions, resulting in inappropriate recommendations' contradicting previously established facts (Fig.1, §1); full-context approaches suffer because 'attention mechanisms degrade over distant tokens' and critical facts get buried among thousands of irrelevant tokens (§1); mitigated by Mem0's selective salient-fact extraction+update pipeline, cutting token cost >90% while improving accuracy (Abstract).
cita: Chhikara et al. (2025). Mem0: Building Production-Ready AI Agents with Scalable Long-Term Memory.
notes: mem_tipos=EPISODICA;SEMANTICA: memory extracted from ongoing conversational exchanges (episodic source) and stored as salient facts/entities+relations (semantic content), §1-2. representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS;VECTOR;GRAFO: base Mem0 stores plain-text facts searched via dense embeddings ('the vector database employs dense embeddings to facilitate efficient similarity search', §2.1); Mem0^g stores memories 'as a directed labeled graph G=(V,E,L)' with entity/relationship embeddings (§2.2). operaciones=WRITE;ADMISION;CONSOLIDACION;OLVIDO;ACTUALIZACION: ALL FIVE explicit -- extraction creates candidate facts (WRITE, §2.1); a tool-call LLM chooses ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP per candidate (ADMISION, §2.1, Algorithm1); an asynchronous module 'periodically refreshes the conversation summary' (CONSOLIDACION, §2.1); DELETE explicitly removes 'memories contradicted by new information' (OLVIDO, §2.1); UPDATE augments existing memories and the graph variant's conflict-resolver 'determines if certain relationships should be obsolete, marking them as invalid' (ACTUALIZACION, §2.1-2.2). trigger=DISCRECIONAL-LLM;EVENTO-DETERMINISTA: 'The LLM itself determines which of four distinct operations to execute' via the tool-call mechanism (§2.1); extraction 'initiates upon ingestion of a new message pair' (§2.1). retrieval=EMBEDDINGS;GRAFO;RANKING: base Mem0 retrieves 'top s semantically similar memories using vector embeddings' (§2.1); Mem0^g's dual retrieval -- entity-centric subgraph traversal plus a semantic-triplet dense-embedding match with relevance-threshold ranking (§2.2). mide_lectura=SI (matches F_screening): LLM-as-a-Judge accuracy across 4 question categories on LOCOMO, Table1. alcance=SESION: LOCOMO's '10 extended conversations...distributed across multiple sessions' (§3.1), explicit cross-session persistence (Fig.1). multiagente=NO: processes 'a pair of messages between either two user participants or a user and an assistant' -- conversational memory for human users, not shared memory among multiple LLM agents. fidelidad_procedencia=SI: explicit conflict-detection -- 'An LLM-based update resolver determines if certain relationships should be obsolete, marking them as invalid rather than physically removing them to enable temporal reasoning' (§2.2); base Mem0's DELETE operation for 'memories contradicted by new information' (§2.1). F=CONSOLIDACION;RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO;COSTO;WRITE;FIDELIDAD (WRITE and FIDELIDAD added vs F_screening: WRITE for the dedicated ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP tool-call architecture, §2.1; FIDELIDAD for the explicit conflict-detection/staleness mechanism, §2.2). evidencia_tipo=ABLATION(Mem0 vs Mem0^g with-vs-without graph memory, 'around 2% higher overall score than the base Mem0 configuration', Abstract)+BENCHMARK-E2E(Table1: LOCOMO vs 6 baseline categories)+MEDICION-COSTO(token consumption and latency measurements). handoff=CONTENIDO: extracted facts/graph persist and are retrieved across sessions (Fig.1 dietary-preference example). plan_estado=NO.
